tagline: The Worlds 2018 war cry that turned a pro's climb into legend.
headline: RISE turned a real champion's climb into an animated epic and became the second most-watched Worlds anthem video on YouTube.
summary: Released on September 26, 2018 as the anthem of the League of Legends World Championship in South Korea, RISE paired The Glitch Mob's production with vocals from Mako and The Word Alive's Telle Smith, and its animated video retold Samsung Galaxy jungler Ambition's six-year climb to the 2017 title, past Perkz, Uzi and finally Faker. The song opened the Incheon final with BOBBY of iKON, passed 180 million YouTube views within three months and now sits at about 425 million, behind only Warriors among Worlds anthems. It returned at the 2023 final in Seoul, and Dot Esports ranks it the best Worlds song ever made.

story.heading: A soundtrack for the top of the ladder
story.body:
In 2018 Riot again worked with Alex Seaver of Mako and songwriter Justin Tranter, who had written *Legends Never Die* for Worlds 2017 with the Riot Music Team. This time it added two very different bands. The Glitch Mob, whose anthemic, hard-hitting electronic sound the team felt fit the brief perfectly, co-produced the track with Riot and Seaver. The Word Alive lent its singer, Telle Smith, to sing alongside Mako, and HEALTH contributed additional production.

In Riot's *Making of RISE* video, the team describes Worlds as the top of the ladder, the peak of millions of hours that players around the world put in, and says it wanted a fight song about climbing a mountain. The Glitch Mob recalled that Riot's first sketches already showed a character scaling a rocky mountain, which felt like their own sound in a nutshell. The chorus nearly beat everyone. One collaborator admits he couldn't hit the big "RISE" himself, and Telle Smith was the one who smashed it, screams included.

story.heading: Ambition's climb
story.body:
*RISE* premiered on League's YouTube channel on September 26, 2018, and the single reached streaming services two days later, shortly before Worlds began on October 1. The video starts in a field of fallen team banners and abandoned champion weapons. A hooded climber picks up Kha'Zix's claws and starts up the mountain. He fights G2's Perkz, as Yasuo, in a wheat field and is hunted by RNG's Uzi, as Vayne, through a canyon of lava. He crosses a frozen battlefield of champion statues beneath the Elder Dragon and passes statues of SK Telecom T1's past titles. At the top, Faker waits as Ryze, rune book in hand.

Near the end, the climber pulls back his hood. He is Kang "Ambition" Chan-yong, who began his pro career in late 2011 as a mid laner, switched to jungle for the 2015 season, and won the 2017 World Championship with Samsung Galaxy by sweeping Faker's SKT 3–0. The video ends with the 2018 contenders starting their own climb.

story.heading: A video built for the pause button
story.body:
Fans went through the video frame by frame, and within four days Leaguepedia had a page collecting their findings. The banners in the opening field include Saigon Jokers, Moscow 5, Cloud9 and Flash Wolves, none of which ever won Worlds. A player frozen in ice nods to Frozen. Faker's rune book carries his old username, 고전파, along with a doodle of broccoli and a Korean caption that translates as "The Unkillable Demon King's fundamental guide to winning Worlds". Three crossed-out pictures in the book were read as a joke about the champions he used to ban in solo queue.

The fights were metaphors rather than replays. Perkz never played Yasuo against Samsung, and Uzi played Tristana, not Vayne, when RNG beat them twice in the 2017 groups. Riot chose each player's signature champion instead, which is a big part of why the video still plays like a love letter to the pro scene.

story.heading: Incheon, November 3, 2018
story.body:
On October 25 Riot released a *RISE* remix featuring BOBBY of iKON, who raps in Korean and English. Nine days later the song opened the final at Incheon Munhak Stadium. Mako and The Word Alive sang on either side of the Summoner's Cup with The Glitch Mob at their rigs behind them, BOBBY rapped from a platform in the middle of the crowd, and Fnatic and Invictus Gaming walked out under their flags while the song was still going. The same ceremony also saw K/DA make its debut with *POP/STARS*.

Invictus Gaming then swept Fnatic 3–0, giving China's LPL its first world title and ending a run of five straight Korean champions. The final drew 99.6 million unique viewers, with 44 million watching at the peak. In China, fans came to see *RISE* as the story of IG's own climb over the mountains to the Summoner's Cup.

story.heading: Two anthems, one autumn
story.body:
Worlds 2018 gave Riot two hits. By December 11, Inven Global reported that *RISE* and *POP/STARS* had each passed 180 million YouTube views. *RISE* has kept climbing since. It had about 280 million views by September 2021, and as of October 2026 its video has 425 million views and 3.3 million likes. That makes it the most-watched Worlds anthem video after Imagine Dragons' *Warriors* and the third most-viewed upload on the League of Legends channel, behind *POP/STARS* and *Warriors*. On Spotify the track has passed 400 million streams.

When The Word Alive released their own version in 2024, Telle Smith called *RISE* the second-biggest Worlds anthem in esports history, and the band's label counted more than 440 million streams by then.

story.heading: Still climbing
story.body:
*RISE* has been reworked several times. In July 2022 the LPL and Zi De Guqin Studio rearranged it for traditional instruments, including the guzheng, pipa and flute, to celebrate Hanfu Day. On November 19, 2023, at the Worlds final in Seoul's Gocheok Sky Dome, the 2018 anthem returned to the opening ceremony, with The Glitch Mob and The Word Alive back on the Worlds stage. For the song's fifth anniversary, The Word Alive released *RISE (REDUX)* on February 23, 2024, a heavier version produced by Erik Ron, and said fans had been asking for it for years.

Critics still rank it at or near the top. Dot Esports puts it first among all Worlds songs, saying it still awaits its challenger, while ONE Esports and Esports Insider both place it second, behind only *Warriors*.

whyItMatters: Its video has about 425M views, more than any other Worlds anthem video except Warriors, and is the third most-viewed upload on the League of Legends YouTube channel.
It turned a real esports story, Ambition's six-year road to the 2017 title, into an animated epic that cast pros like Perkz, Uzi and Faker as mythic rivals and packed in pro-scene references.
It opened the Worlds 2018 final in Incheon with The Glitch Mob, Mako, The Word Alive and BOBBY of iKON, at the same ceremony where K/DA debuted, before a final watched by 99.6M unique viewers.
It reached far beyond the game client: more than 400M Spotify streams, and about 440M streams across services by early 2024.
It has kept coming back: as a traditional-instrument arrangement from the LPL in 2022, on the Worlds 2023 final stage in Seoul, and as The Word Alive's RISE (REDUX) in 2024.
Critics still put it at or near the top: first in Dot Esports' ranking of every Worlds song, second at ONE Esports and Esports Insider.

communityMoments.title: Behind the song
communityMoments.description: Riot's Making of RISE video showed the Riot Music Team, The Glitch Mob, Mako and The Word Alive building a fight song around the image of climbing a mountain.

communityMoments.title: Fans decode every frame
communityMoments.description: Leaguepedia's page of fan findings catalogued the video's easter eggs, including fallen team banners, Frozen trapped in ice, and Faker's rune book with his old username, a broccoli doodle and a 'guide to winning Worlds'.

communityMoments.title: BOBBY joins the climb
communityMoments.description: Riot released a RISE remix featuring iKON's BOBBY, who raps in both Korean and English, ahead of the Incheon final.

communityMoments.title: Opening the Worlds 2018 final
communityMoments.description: The Glitch Mob, Mako, The Word Alive and BOBBY performed RISE at Incheon Munhak Stadium as Fnatic and Invictus Gaming walked out, in the same ceremony where K/DA debuted POP/STARS.

communityMoments.title: 180 million in eleven weeks
communityMoments.description: Inven Global reported that RISE and POP/STARS had each passed 180 million YouTube views, while the final drew 99.6 million unique viewers.

communityMoments.title: IG's mountain
communityMoments.description: Because Invictus Gaming won Worlds 2018, Chinese fans came to see RISE as the story of IG climbing over the mountains to the title, according to Sohu.

communityMoments.title: Back on the Worlds stage
communityMoments.description: Five years later RISE returned at the Worlds 2023 Finals opening ceremony at Gocheok Sky Dome in Seoul, with The Glitch Mob performing it again.

communityMoments.title: The Word Alive's RISE (REDUX)
communityMoments.description: For the fifth anniversary, The Word Alive released their own heavier version, saying fans had asked for it for years.

keyMoments.label: A field of fallen banners
keyMoments.description: The video opens under a glaring sun on a field of fallen team banners and abandoned champion weapons.

keyMoments.label: The climber arms himself
keyMoments.description: The hooded climber picks up Kha'Zix's claws from the battlefield and heads for the mountain.

keyMoments.label: First chorus: Perkz's Yasuo
keyMoments.description: G2's Perkz appears as Yasuo, and his duel with the climber in a wheat field carries the first chorus.

keyMoments.label: Second chorus: Uzi's Vayne
keyMoments.description: RNG's Uzi, as Vayne, peers out from his hood behind red-tinted glasses, then hunts the climber through a canyon of red lava.

keyMoments.label: Bridge: under the Elder Dragon
keyMoments.description: The Elder Dragon glides over a sea of clouds, then over a frozen battlefield of champion statues, as the quiet bridge builds.

keyMoments.label: Faker at the summit
keyMoments.description: Past statues of SKT's world titles, Faker waits at the summit in a red jacket, reading his rune book.

keyMoments.label: Final chorus: Rune Prison
keyMoments.description: Faker, as Ryze, traps the climber in a cage of glowing runes. Then a golden blast tears across the summit.

keyMoments.label: The reveal: Ambition
keyMoments.description: The climber reaches the statue of the 2017 champion and pulls back his hood. He is Samsung Galaxy's Ambition.

keyMoments.label: The next climb
keyMoments.description: Under a night sky dominated by the Worlds emblem, the 2018 contenders start up the volcano toward the next crown.

keyMoments.label: RISE opens the 2018 final
keyMoments.description: Mako and The Word Alive take the Incheon Munhak Stadium stage in front of The Glitch Mob's rigs as RISE kicks off the Worlds 2018 Finals opening ceremony.

keyMoments.label: The Glitch Mob live
keyMoments.description: A member of The Glitch Mob plays the song live at the band's on-stage rig in front of the stadium crowd.

keyMoments.label: Around the Summoner's Cup
keyMoments.description: Singers and a guitarist line up on either side of the Summoner's Cup as pyrotechnics go off behind them.

keyMoments.label: BOBBY in the crowd
keyMoments.description: iKON's BOBBY delivers his remix verse from a platform in the middle of the crowd.

keyMoments.label: The finalists walk out
keyMoments.description: Fnatic and Invictus Gaming walk out under their flags while the song is still playing.

keyMoments.label: RISE returns in 2023
keyMoments.description: Five years later, RISE comes back during the Worlds 2023 Finals opening ceremony at Gocheok Sky Dome. Its first verse starts at about 7:20.

featuredClip.description: Final chorus: Faker, as Ryze, traps the hooded Ambition in a cage of glowing runes and raises his rune book. After a white flash, Ambition grins in golden light as a golden blast erupts across the summit.
